item.summary: fix(dns): keep wide-area SOA serial monotonic across skew and rollover (#124144) * fix(dns): keep wide-area SOA serial monotonic across skew and rollover nextSerial returned the fresh YYYYMMDDNN base whenever the existing serial did not start with today's date, even when that base was smaller than the existing serial. DNS secondaries compare serials with sequence-space arithmetic (RFC 1035 §3.3.1), so a regression silently skips the zone transfer and the updated records never propagate. Two real triggers: 1. Clock skew / manual edit leaves a future-dated serial (e.g. 2027010101). On 2026-03-13 the base 2026031301 is written, below the existing serial. 2. A same-day counter past 99 (2026031399 + 1 = 2026031400) corrupts the date prefix; the next same-day write falls back to 2026031301, again below the existing serial. Guard the next value with Math.max(candidate, existingSerial + 1) so the serial is always strictly greater than the existing one. The branch for a matching today prefix still increments by one; only the regression path changes. Adds two regression tests covering both triggers; both fail against the previous implementation. * fix(dns): use RFC 1982 bounded serial arithm
